blocks.content: In Inheritance, you saw Dog override Animal’s makeSound(). Polymorphism is the payoff of that setup: the ability for the exact same method call to produce genuinely different behavior, depending on what object is actually behind it.
The word literally means "many forms," one call, many possible behaviors, and it comes in two distinct flavors that are easy to mix up.
1. Introduction & Why It Matters

Polymorphism means the same method call can behave differently depending on either the actual object it runs on (runtime polymorphism, via overriding) or the types of arguments passed to it (compile-time polymorphism, via overloading).

Without polymorphism, code that needs to handle many related types ends up as a long chain of "if this type, do X, else if that type, do Y" checks. Every time a new type is added, that chain has to be found and updated everywhere it appears. Polymorphism replaces that chain with one call that automatically does the right thing.
2. Real-Life Analogy
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884646813-259371536.png
blocks.alt: Pressing the same power button on a TV, an AC, and a speaker, each responding completely differently

blocks.content: Press "power" on a TV, an AC, and a speaker, the exact same action, three completely different responses: a screen lighting up, cool air starting to flow, audio powering on. The instruction is identical, the behavior depends entirely on the device receiving it.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884648587-826515122.png
blocks.alt: The same play instruction producing completely different physical actions on a guitar, piano and drum

blocks.content: Tell a guitarist, a pianist, and a drummer to "play," and each does something entirely different with their instrument. One instruction, three different realizations, exactly the shape of polymorphism.
3. Problem It Solves & Definition
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884649986-545083416.png
blocks.alt: A long if-else type-checking chain replaced by one polymorphic method call

blocks.content: Polymorphism solves the problem of type-checking chains. Without it, calculating area for a list of mixed shapes would need something like "if shape is a Circle, do this math, else if shape is a Square, do that math," repeated everywhere shapes are processed. With polymorphism, that entire chain collapses into one line: shape.area().

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.content: Polymorphism is the ability of a single method call to exhibit different behavior depending on the actual type of the object it is invoked on (runtime polymorphism, via method overriding) or the types of the arguments passed to it (compile-time polymorphism, via method overloading).
4. Key Terminology

["Polymorphism: one call, many possible behaviors, literally \"many forms.\"","Runtime polymorphism: achieved through method overriding, resolved based on the object’s actual class at runtime.","Compile-time polymorphism: achieved through method overloading, resolved by the compiler based on argument types.","Method overloading: multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists in the same class.","Upcasting: treating a subclass object through a superclass or interface reference, which is what enables runtime polymorphism."]
items: Polymorphism: one call, many possible behaviors, literally "many forms."
Runtime polymorphism: achieved through method overriding, resolved based on the object’s actual class at runtime.
Compile-time polymorphism: achieved through method overloading, resolved by the compiler based on argument types.
Method overloading: multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists in the same class.
Upcasting: treating a subclass object through a superclass or interface reference, which is what enables runtime polymorphism.

blocks.content: 5. Visual Diagram
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884651469-42099753.png
blocks.alt: A Shape array holding a Circle and a Square, the same loop calling area on each with different results

blocks.content: The loop below has exactly one line calling shape.area(). It never checks what kind of shape it is, yet Circle’s area formula and Square’s area formula both run correctly, each object simply knows how to compute its own area.
6. Syntax & Code Example

Overriding (runtime polymorphism) reuses the same method name and signature in a subclass. Overloading (compile-time polymorphism) reuses the same method name in the SAME class with a different parameter list:
This example demonstrates both kinds of polymorphism together, a Shape hierarchy for runtime polymorphism, and an overloaded Calculator.add() for compile-time polymorphism:
7. Code Breakdown

["Shape[] shapes = { new Circle(5), new Square(4) }; the array is declared as Shape, but each element is really a more specific subclass.","for (Shape shape : shapes) { shape.area(); } this single line correctly computes a circle’s area and a square’s area, because each object’s own overridden area() runs.","calc.add(2, 3) the compiler sees two int arguments and picks the int-int add() overload, at compile time, before the program ever runs.","calc.add(2.5, 3.5) the compiler sees two double arguments and picks the double-double add() overload instead, a completely separate decision from the first call."]
items: Shape[] shapes = { new Circle(5), new Square(4) }; the array is declared as Shape, but each element is really a more specific subclass.
for (Shape shape : shapes) { shape.area(); } this single line correctly computes a circle’s area and a square’s area, because each object’s own overridden area() runs.
calc.add(2, 3) the compiler sees two int arguments and picks the int-int add() overload, at compile time, before the program ever runs.
calc.add(2.5, 3.5) the compiler sees two double arguments and picks the double-double add() overload instead, a completely separate decision from the first call.

9. Behind the Scenes (Two Different Mechanisms)
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884654531-603100704.png
blocks.alt: Overloading resolved by the compiler using argument types, overriding resolved by the runtime using the actual object

blocks.content: These two kinds of polymorphism are resolved by completely different parts of the toolchain, which is exactly why they are so often confused.
9.1 Overloading Is Resolved at Compile Time
blocks.text: 9.1 Overloading Is Resolved at Compile Time

blocks.content: When the compiler sees calc.add(2, 3), it looks at the argument types (int, int) and picks the matching add() overload right then, before the program ever runs. This is why overloading is called compile-time (or static) polymorphism.
9.2 Overriding Is Resolved at Runtime

When the JVM executes shape.area(), it cannot know in advance which area() to run just by looking at the declared Shape type. It checks the object’s actual class the moment the line executes, this is why overriding is called runtime (or dynamic) polymorphism.
10. Real-World Use Cases & Industry Examples
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884656051-901552502.png
blocks.alt: One polymorphic method call behaving differently across e-commerce, banking, social and gaming domains

blocks.content: ["E-commerce: every Discount type (PercentageDiscount, FlatDiscount) applies itself differently through one shared apply() call.","Banking: every AccountType calculates interest differently through one shared calculateInterest() call.","Social Media: every Notification type (LikeNotification, CommentNotification) renders differently through one shared render() call.","Gaming: every Character subclass attacks differently through one shared attack() call."]
items: E-commerce: every Discount type (PercentageDiscount, FlatDiscount) applies itself differently through one shared apply() call.
Banking: every AccountType calculates interest differently through one shared calculateInterest() call.
Social Media: every Notification type (LikeNotification, CommentNotification) renders differently through one shared render() call.
Gaming: every Character subclass attacks differently through one shared attack() call.

blocks.content: One of the most common examples of runtime polymorphism is something you have already used constantly without necessarily naming it:
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/lld-images/1784884657552-691602564.png
blocks.alt: System.out.println calling toString on any object, with each class producing its own different text

blocks.content: Every Java class inherits a toString() method from Object, and can override it. System.out.println(someObject) always calls the exact same line internally, someObject.toString(), yet it prints completely different text depending on which class actually overrode toString(), pure runtime polymorphism, everywhere in the language.
11. Advantages & Limitations

{"headers":["Advantages","Limitations"],"rows":[["New types can be added without touching any existing type-checking logic.","Runtime polymorphism has a small performance cost compared to a direct, non-virtual method call."],["Client code stays simple: one call site instead of a growing chain of type checks.","Overuse of overloading with very similar signatures can make it genuinely unclear which overload will run."],["Overriding and overloading together give flexibility for both \"different objects\" and \"different argument shapes.\"","Runtime polymorphism requires a real IS-A relationship (inheritance or an interface) to exist first."]]}
12. Common Mistakes & Best Practices
12.1 Common Mistakes

["Confusing overloading and overriding, remember: overloading is same class, different parameters, resolved at compile time; overriding is subclass, same signature, resolved at runtime.","Writing overloaded methods with subtly ambiguous signatures (like add(int, long) and add(long, int)) that confuse callers about which one actually runs.","Forgetting that fields are NOT polymorphic in Java, only methods are, accessing a field through a superclass reference always uses the superclass’s field.","Re-implementing a type-checking if-else chain out of habit, when the types involved already share a common supertype that could just be overridden instead."]
items: Confusing overloading and overriding, remember: overloading is same class, different parameters, resolved at compile time; overriding is subclass, same signature, resolved at runtime.
Writing overloaded methods with subtly ambiguous signatures (like add(int, long) and add(long, int)) that confuse callers about which one actually runs.
Forgetting that fields are NOT polymorphic in Java, only methods are, accessing a field through a superclass reference always uses the superclass’s field.
Re-implementing a type-checking if-else chain out of habit, when the types involved already share a common supertype that could just be overridden instead.

blocks.content: 12.2 Best Practices

["Reach for runtime polymorphism (overriding) whenever a growing type-checking chain starts to appear in your code.","Keep overloaded signatures clearly distinct in purpose, not just technically different, to avoid confusing call sites.","Always mark intentionally overridden methods with @Override so the compiler catches signature mistakes.","Design new types to fit an existing supertype’s contract whenever possible, so they automatically work with existing polymorphic call sites."]
items: Reach for runtime polymorphism (overriding) whenever a growing type-checking chain starts to appear in your code.
Keep overloaded signatures clearly distinct in purpose, not just technically different, to avoid confusing call sites.
Always mark intentionally overridden methods with @Override so the compiler catches signature mistakes.
Design new types to fit an existing supertype’s contract whenever possible, so they automatically work with existing polymorphic call sites.

blocks.content: 13. Key Takeaways & Cheat Sheet

["Polymorphism lets one method call behave differently, either based on the actual object (runtime) or the argument types (compile-time).","Runtime polymorphism comes from overriding, and is resolved by checking the object’s real class when the line actually executes.","Compile-time polymorphism comes from overloading, and is resolved by the compiler before the program ever runs.","Polymorphism replaces growing if-else type-checking chains with a single, stable call site.","toString(), called through println(), is a runtime polymorphism example you have likely already used constantly."]
items: Polymorphism lets one method call behave differently, either based on the actual object (runtime) or the argument types (compile-time).
Runtime polymorphism comes from overriding, and is resolved by checking the object’s real class when the line actually executes.
Compile-time polymorphism comes from overloading, and is resolved by the compiler before the program ever runs.
Polymorphism replaces growing if-else type-checking chains with a single, stable call site.
toString(), called through println(), is a runtime polymorphism example you have likely already used constantly.

blocks.title: Interview tip
blocks.content: If asked "what is the difference between overloading and overriding," the fastest correct answer is: overloading is same method name, different parameters, in the same class, resolved at compile time, overriding is same method name and parameters, in a subclass, resolved at runtime based on the actual object.
